hypothesis: A model trained from scratch can encode similarity by which tree leaves two rows share. Query a disjoint store of real training outcomes to learn model residuals among similar rows. Previous categorical-distance neighbours and broad group-level residuals did not measure this learned supervised representation.
data: Same bound 4061-row fitting packet, 808 nomination, 817 and 807 check packets used for development. No official validation, formal test, H2, external labels or API. Two fitted context-tree encoders, splitting exact duplicate groups. Each side is a reference set only for the tree trained on the opposite side. Retain a sealed prior full-training tree's probability as a base; only residuals from rows genuinely held out from their encoder are transferred.
implementation: Average contributions from two encoders. Subsample at most 128 evenly spaced CatBoost trees. Leaf overlap defines similarity. Use the 32 or 96 nearest rows, break ties by including all rows at the boundary, weight similarity to power eight, apply a shrinkage constant equal to one quarter of the nominal neighbour count on effective sample size and clip probabilities to [.001,.999]. No feature or label name routing.
election: Use the existing generic nomination and check protocol: choose retain or a candidate's weight from 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1 against the previously strongest research pair, using nomination only. Require nonnegative changes on each check and at least +0.003 pooled to run a bigger blind test. Report raw counts versus the original single tree separately, no promotion from that descriptive comparison. Exact protocol tracked with the candidate hashes.
